name: 柯沃尔
src: 纷争纪/纷争纪时段_七_号角的年月.md:2202
who: Kovol, called the Heel-Gatherer, a demon-kin priest who serves the demon god called the Last of the Line, from a scattered clan of the western edge of the deadlands, ninety-nine and looking about forty: about 176 cm, lean and spare. Grey-blue skin, with fine ripple marks like wind on sand running from the side of the neck up behind the ears. Very short hair, pale gold faded to the colour of sand. Indigo eyes. A pair of short horns; the left one is broken off flat at the root (on the viewer's right when he faces us). The tendon of his left heel was cut long ago, leaving a straight scar across it; he walks with a white bone staff and goes barefoot. A grey cloak covered from collar to hem with patches of sand-lifted footprints. No jewellery. A slow, courteous, quietly certain air.
build: 176 cm, lean and spare, a slight limp on the left leg.
palette: sand grey and pale dune gold, grey-blue skin, indigo, bone white
casual: His priest's dress: the long grey cloak worn closed, its whole surface from collar to hem stitched with patch after patch of footprints peeled up with their sand, like a quilt of sandy tracks, the first patch at the collar his own; under it a plain sand-coloured linen robe closing down the front with bone buttons, a rope belt; bare feet. He leans on the white bone staff in his right hand, a calm, courteous look.
private: At a small fire on the dunes: the footprint cloak folded over one arm, the sand-coloured linen robe, bare feet. He threads a bone needle with fine white thread, a quiet, patient look.
battle: Opening the rite before the wounded god: the footprint cloak thrown back from the shoulders, its sand patches glowing faintly white along every seam, the linen robe belted tight, bone-plate bracers, a long white thread trailing from the bone needle in his left hand. He sets the white bone staff to strike the ground in his right hand, a still, merciful, unyielding look.
formal: At the god's feet on the night of the rite: a long pale sand-coloured robe to the ankles with a soft high collar, closing down the front with bone buttons, a narrow white stole stitched with rows of tiny footprints, the footprint cloak over his shoulders, bare feet. He holds the bone staff upright before him with both hands, a grave, serene look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the indigo eyes looking at the viewer gently, the broken horn stump clear, a bone needle with a glowing white thread raised near his face. Cold blue dusk light over the dunes from one side, the pale white glow of the thread on the other. Foreground blur: drifting sand, the edge of the footprint-patched cloak, a line of footprints vanishing into sand.

name: 奎塔姆
src: 纷争纪/纷争纪时段_七_号角的年月.md:2222
who: Quitam, called the Bowl-Bearer, a demon-kin of the Long-Lived line, First Seat of the Blood-Oath faction, who has borne the head bowl at eleven blood feasts, about two thousand three hundred years old and looking a little past fifty: very tall, about 194 cm, gaunt, with a slight stoop from carrying the bowl for a thousand years. Pale grey-white skin. Raven-blue-black hair combed straight back. NO horns (the Long-Lived have no horns, scales or tail); slightly pointed ears; a thin circlet of dark red oath ribbons bound around the brow, their ends hanging behind. The right eye violet; the left eye is gone, the socket covered by a smooth round disc of polished black clay (on the viewer's right when he faces us). Around his neck eleven broken bowl rims threaded on a dark red leather cord, one overlapping the next like an unclosed shackle, clinking at every step. No other jewellery. A flat, slow, unshakable air.
face: FACE, as in the references: a long, gaunt man's face of a little past fifty, lines at the eye and mouth, a single violet right eye, the left eye socket (on the viewer's right when he faces us) covered by a smooth round disc of polished black clay, raven-blue-black hair combed back, thin pale lips; pale grey-white skin with very little shading.
build: 194 cm, very tall and gaunt, long-armed, the shoulders slightly stooped.
palette: blood red and oath crimson, pale ash grey, raven blue-black, black clay, violet
casual: His first-seat vestments: a long pale ash-grey linen robe to the ankles, closing down the front with a row of black clay buttons, fitted sleeves with dark red cuffs, a long dark red stole embroidered with a row of small bowls hanging from the shoulders, a narrow belt, soft dark boots; the eleven bowl rims at his throat. He holds the old black clay head bowl in his left hand, a flat, unhurried look.
private: Alone in his tent: a long plain grey wool robe closing down the front with buttons, no stole, soft boots, the bowl rims still at his throat. He polishes the black clay head bowl with a cloth held in both hands, a still, withdrawn look.
battle: Leading a hundred thousand beneath the siege temples: a long dark red war vestment over a coat of black lacquered scale, sculpted black pauldrons engraved with rows of bowls, the oath ribbons at his brow streaming behind, the eleven bowl rims at his throat glowing a dull blood red. He holds the black clay head bowl high in his left hand and strikes its rim with the knuckles of his right, a ring of red light spreading from it, a cold, commanding look.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: tall and commanding, the shoulders squared despite the stoop, the feet planted, the black clay head bowl lifted in his left hand and the knuckles of his right raised to strike its rim, a cold expression; he carries no blade.
formal: Bearing the head bowl at the hundred-year feast: a floor-length dark red robe with ash-grey borders, closing down the front with black clay buttons, fitted sleeves, a soft high collar, a long black stole hung with small blood-red seals, fresh oath ribbons bound around his brow, the eleven bowl rims at his throat. He holds the black clay head bowl level before his chest in both hands, a grave, solemn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the single violet eye looking at the viewer without warmth, the clay disc over the left socket catching the light, the eleven bowl rims at his throat. Red firelight from a feast below on one side, cold blue night on the other. Foreground blur: the rim of a full red bowl, drifting embers, a dark red oath ribbon.

name: 兰博尔德
src: 纷争纪/纷争纪时段_七_号角的年月.md:2244
who: Rambold, called Twisted Key, a human, Stringmaster of the winding yard on this stretch of the southern wall, keeper of thousands of clockwork soldiers, eighty-six and looking a little past fifty for his rank: about 179 cm, solid and square-shouldered. Rust-red short hair, white at the temples. Brass-coloured eyes. The upper half of his left ear is missing, torn off long ago by a snapping mainspring (on the viewer's right when he faces us). The thumb and forefinger of his right hand carry calluses so thick they no longer close. At his belt hangs a string of winding keys rusted solid, the first one twisted into a spiral. No goggles and no jewellery. A terse, practical air; he tilts his good ear toward a sound and tells you how many turns are left.
face: FACE, as in the references: a square man's face of a little past fifty, lines at the eyes and mouth, brass-coloured eyes, rust-red brows, rust-red short hair white at the temples, the upper half of the left ear missing (on the viewer's right when he faces us); fair skin.
build: 179 cm, solid and square-shouldered, thick forearms.
palette: rust red and brass, oiled leather brown, wall grey, copper wire
casual: His winding-yard dress: an old leather apron with a row of small pockets across the chest holding wrenches and brass tuning pins, over a grey wool wall coat with the cuffs bound tight in copper wire, dark trousers and heavy boots; the string of rusted winding keys at his belt, the spiral-twisted key first; a plain long knife in a sheath at the other hip. He tilts his head with the good ear toward a sound, a terse, weighing look.
private: At the water spring outside the south gate: the apron off, a plain long-sleeved wool shirt with the sleeves rolled, a dark waistcoat, trousers and boots. He holds a wooden water ladle in his callused right hand, a tired, quiet look.
battle: Riding at the head of the risen machines: an oilcloth cloak over a leather brigandine riveted with brass plates and old clockwork parts, a pauldron made from a clockwork soldier's shoulder plate, the cuffs bound in copper wire, the string of rusted keys at his belt. He grips a long iron winding crank in both hands, its handle as long as his arm and its key-head glowing with a dull ash-grey light, a hard, set look.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: braced and set, the feet planted, gripping the long iron winding crank in both hands across his body, a hard, set expression.
formal: Before the garrison of the next wall city: a clean grey wool wall coat brushed and buttoned to the collar, the winding-yard badge of a brass key over a gear on the chest, a dark sash, polished boots, the string of rusted keys at his belt. He stands upright with the hands at his sides, a grave, stubborn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the brass-coloured eyes looking at the viewer through rain, the torn left ear in the light, the spiral-twisted key held up near his face. Cold blue rain light from one side, the orange of a gate fire on the other. Foreground blur: rain streaks, grey ash on the wind, the dull brass shoulder of a kneeling clockwork soldier.
